issues.legal_issue: The character of property for a declaration as evacuee property is determined by whether it was property of an evacuee when the person migrated, and a later vesting of title in an insolvency receiver does not prevent the declaration.
material_facts: The property belonged to the person when he migrated to Pakistan and he was treated as an evacuee.
After the migration, creditors petitioned for insolvency; the person was adjudicated insolvent and the estate vested in an Official Receiver, with the vesting relating back to the petition.
The Custodian issued notice and declared the property evacuee property after the insolvency vesting.
issues.conclusion: The declaration was not invalid merely because the property had vested in the Official Receiver before the declaration; the Custodian could determine its character by reference to whether it was the evacuee’s property at migration.
issues.legal_principle: Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, ss. 2(f) and 7(1), construed liberally in light of the Act’s provisions and purpose, require the authority to consider whether the property was evacuee property, including property of an evacuee, rather than whether the evacuee retained title on the date of declaration. Sections 7(2) and 40 reflect the legislative purpose of preventing transfers from defeating the Act. Section 7(1A), added retrospectively after Ebrahim Aboobaker v. Tek Chand Dolwani, [1953] SCR 691, addresses continuation of pending proceedings after death. The later vesting in an insolvency receiver under the Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920, ss. 27 and 28(7), does not alter the property’s relevant character for this purpose.

rule.if: appeal_from_evacuee_property_declaration and subject_was_evacuee_on_migration and property_belonged_to_subject_on_migration and insolvency_receiver_acquired_title_before_declaration

predicates.appeal_from_evacuee_property_declaration: The matter is an appeal concerning a declaration that property is evacuee property.
predicates.subject_was_evacuee_on_migration: The person whose property is in issue migrated in circumstances that made the person an evacuee.
predicates.property_belonged_to_subject_on_migratio: The property belonged to that person when the person migrated.
predicates.insolvency_receiver_acquired_title_befor: An insolvency receiver acquired title to the property before the evacuee-property declaration was made.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an evacuee-property declaration, the property belonged to a person who became an evacuee upon migration, and an insolvency receiver acquired title before the declaration, the declaration may rest on the property’s character at migration.

issues.legal_issue: Retrospective vesting in the Custodian under the evacuee-property scheme cannot determine whether the declaration that triggers that vesting was valid.
material_facts: The Custodian’s declaration was made after the insolvency adjudication and receiver’s vesting of the estate.
The Custodian relied on the asserted retrospective effect of the declaration to claim that vesting in the Custodian took priority.
issues.conclusion: The retrospective vesting consequence could operate only after a valid declaration and could not be used to construe or establish the validity of the declaration itself.
issues.legal_principle: Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, s. 8(1)(a), makes vesting in the Custodian a statutory consequence of a valid declaration under s. 7(1); it therefore cannot determine whether the declaration was validly made.

predicates.evacuee_property_declaration_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether property was validly declared evacuee property.
predicates.custodian_claimed_retroactive_vesting_af: The Custodian relied on vesting that would operate retrospectively after a declaration.
predicates.validity_of_declaration_was_disputed: A party challenged whether the declaration was validly made.

issues.definition: Where the validity of an evacuee-property declaration is disputed, retrospective vesting that follows the declaration cannot itself establish the declaration’s validity.

issues.legal_issue: The overriding clause in the evacuee-property legislation does not displace insolvency vesting provisions when the two statutory schemes are not inconsistent.
material_facts: The insolvency adjudication vested the insolvent’s property in the Official Receiver from the date of the creditors’ petition.
The parties also relied on the evacuee-property legislation, which provided for vesting in the Custodian following a declaration.
issues.conclusion: The insolvency provisions were not inconsistent with the evacuee-property legislation, so the overriding clause did not displace them.
issues.legal_principle: Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, s. 4(1), gives that Act priority only over inconsistent laws. Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920, ss. 27 and 28(7), provide for property to vest in the Official Receiver from the presentation of the insolvency petition; those provisions are not inconsistent with ss. 7 and 8 of the evacuee-property legislation.

predicates.proceeding_involves_evacuee_property_and: The proceeding involves both an evacuee-property claim and an insolvency receiver’s claim to property.
predicates.insolvency_order_relates_back_to_credito: The insolvency order causes the property to vest in the receiver from the date creditors presented their petition.

issues.definition: When a proceeding involves both claims and insolvency vesting relates back to the creditors’ petition, the insolvency vesting is not displaced unless the two statutory schemes are inconsistent.

issues.legal_issue: The rule that proceedings cannot continue after an alleged evacuee dies does not apply when the alleged evacuee remains alive during the inquiry.
material_facts: The alleged evacuee was alive when the Custodian conducted the inquiry and made the declaration.
The respondent relied on an earlier decision concerning proceedings in which the alleged evacuee had died while the inquiry was pending.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision did not govern this case because the alleged evacuee was alive during the inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Ebrahim Aboobaker v. Tek Chand Dolwani, [1953] SCR 691, concerned the impossibility of continuing an inquiry after the alleged evacuee died; it does not apply where the alleged evacuee is alive during the inquiry. Section 7(1A) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, provides for continuation of pending proceedings after a person’s death.

predicates.evacuee_property_declaration_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a declaration that a person’s property is evacuee property.
predicates.alleged_evacuee_alive_during_inquiry: The person whose status and property are under inquiry is alive while the inquiry is conducted.

issues.definition: In a proceeding concerning an evacuee-property declaration, if the alleged evacuee is alive during the inquiry, the rule concerning an inquiry interrupted by the person’s death does not bar the proceeding.
